prompt: Two friends stand $100$ m apart on a flat field and both look up at a drone. From friend $A$ the angle to the drone is $30^\circ$; from friend $B$ it is $60^\circ$. That makes the angle at the drone $90^\circ$. How many meters is the drone from friend $B$?
hint: The $100$ m gap sits ACROSS from the drone's $90^\circ$ angle — that is your matching pair.

hints.text: The $100$ m gap sits ACROSS from the drone's $90^\circ$ angle — that is your matching pair.
The side from $B$ to the drone sits across from angle $A = 30^\circ$. So $\frac{a}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{100}{\sin 90^\circ}$.

explanation: Label the triangle: the two friends and the drone are the corners.
The $100$ m side is across from the $90^\circ$ drone angle, so use that pair.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw it in words first
steps: Sketch a flat line with friend A on the left and friend B on the right, 100 m apart.
Draw both sight lines up to the drone. The steeper 60° line belongs to friend B, so friend B is CLOSER.
Closer means the answer must be less than 100 m, and 50 m passes that sanity check.

alternativeExplanations.title: Which side goes with which angle
steps: Big angle, big side across from it. Order the angles: 30° < 60° < 90°.
So the shortest side is across from 30°, which is exactly the B-to-drone distance you want.
The 100 m side is across the biggest angle, and 50 is the smallest of the three — the sizes line up.
